messages:
alex_support: Hey team — we have a production customer hitting a streaming hang after auth rotation. Generator yields first partial tokens then never resumes. Seen on Python SDK v0.11.7. Logs attached below. Anyone seen this? cc @sre @devex :eyes:

sara_sre: can you paste minimal repro + the raw stream bytes/logs?

alex_support: repro steps are short: open stream, after ~30s we rotate creds (internal KMS), server returns refresh OK but client stream stalls. Heap of logs: 

```
2025-06-01T14:02:17Z INFO stream opened
2025-06-01T14:02:22Z DEBUG recv: b'data: {"delta":"Hel'
2025-06-01T14:02:22Z DEBUG recv: b''  # next chunk never arrives
2025-06-01T14:02:23Z DEBUG auth: rotate start
2025-06-01T14:02:23Z INFO auth: refresh token ok (200)
2025-06-01T14:02:24Z DEBUG recv: b'\n'  # keepalive
# generator never yields complete message, client code stuck in for-loop
```

Also saw a 401 briefly during rotation in a different trace, then 200 on retry.

kevin_devex: which exact pip package/version? there were parser changes in 0.12.x that touched SSE buffering.

alex_support: pin shows `redwood-sdk==0.11.7` in requirements. Customer hasn't upgraded.

sujay_eng: likely parser state machine doesn't recover from mid-event auth transient. If the HTTP connection emits a 401 followed by reconnect that reuses the same socket stream boundary, partial bytes can be left in the buffer. Parser stays in "in-event" state and never emits because delimiter was lost.

maria_support: interesting. any quick workaround for the customer other than a full SDK upgrade? they're on a managed plan and need a immediate mitigation.

kevin_devex: temporary mitigation options:
- set a short stream-level timeout (client-side) so generator raises and you can recreate the stream after rotation
- disable credential auto-rotate for that workload until patch applied
- add application-level keepalive that flushes/validates event completions

alex_support: reproducer script (minimal):
```
from redwood import StreamingClient
c = StreamingClient(api_key=..., stream_timeout=None)
for ev in c.stream("model-x", prompt):
    print(ev)
```
Trigger rotation 10s after stream starts and observe hang.

sara_sre: can you attach the exact raw bytes from tcpdump or server side chunk log? need to see interleaving of 401/200 and chunk boundaries.

alex_support: attached tcp dump excerpt in ticket. It shows the chunk with partial JSON followed by an auth challenge and then a 200 that resumes without the newline.

sujay_eng: we'll prioritize: plan is to make parser tolerant to mid-stream auth responses: on auth transient (401/reauth) or connection control codes we reset internal event buffer and raise a StreamAuthError to the generator instead of silently waiting. That will let callers handle a reconnect. PR ETA 48h, patch release target v0.12.5.

kevin_devex: also flagging that older SDKs (<=0.11.x) don't expose the stream_timeout option by default — we should add a compatibility notice in release notes and an interim patch backport. @maria_support can you escalate to sales/customer success for an outage credit check?

maria_support: yes opened escalation to CS.

eng-bot: Incident INC-2034 created for streaming auth hang. Priority P2. Linked ticket: https://redwood/issues/INC-2034

alex_support: thanks — customer confirmed workaround (short client timeout + auto-reconnect) works for now. Please keep me posted on PRs.

sujay_eng: will post PR and a minimal test that simulates mid-chunk 401 -> 200 transitions. Also adding an integration test that asserts generator raises a recoverable exception rather than hanging.

kevin_devex: temporary snip for users until patch: upgrade to our nightly wheel `pip install redwood-sdk==0.12.4.dev202506` or wrap streaming loop with a watchdog timer to recreate stream on stalls.

alex_support: posting repro and tcp dump to the incident ticket. thanks all :thumbsup:
